title: Security Testing for AI
description: Title slide for Lecture 7 of the AI Testing Academy series.

title: Learning Objectives
description: Five learning objectives covering attack surface, injection, data leakage, adversarial inputs, and building a security suite.

title: The AI Attack Surface
description: Overview of where AI systems are exposed to attack: prompts, tools, training data, and outputs.

title: OWASP LLM Top 10
description: Overview of the OWASP Top 10 for Large Language Model applications.

description: The cost of not testing AI security: real incidents and consequences.

title: System Prompt Leakage

title: Jailbreaking Techniques
description: A taxonomy of jailbreaking techniques: role-play, encoding, hypothetical framing, and token smuggling.

description: Recording actual token spend vs cap for DoW tests in Supabase and asserting all tests respected the cap.

description: Querying Supabase for adversarial test results over time to detect regressions in robustness.

description: How attackers evade content classifiers and guardrails with minimal perturbation.

description: Key lessons from the adversarial inputs and robustness section.

description: Architecture of an automated red-team test harness: YAML prompt library, LLM judge, and Supabase persistence.

description: Recording guardrail test results per category and build in Supabase and computing pass rates.

description: Querying Supabase for weekly security findings and computing MTTR to track team response velocity.

description: Three principles for building an effective AI security test suite.

title: Check Your Understanding
description: Four discussion questions covering injection surfaces, score regression, incident response, and rate limiting.

description: Four key takeaways: cover all injection surfaces, filter outputs, persist results for trending, and cap every resource dimension.
